messages:
maria.g: Quick check — we need a canonical statement for fallback order when both an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and `X-Org-ID`/`X-Project-ID` are present. Some SDKs currently infer org from key, others prefer explicit header. Can we agree and document examples?

aj: Short answer: explicit header wins. If `X-Org-ID` present, use it. If absent, fall back to key-scoped org. But we need clear rules for proxy-stripping and legacy headers. :thinking:

devon: Agreed on explicit wins. Edge: what if header org does not match key's org? Reject or allow? I think reject with 403 and telemetry tag `auth_mismatch` so callers can migrate.

aj: +1 for 403 + telemetry `auth_mismatch`. 401 should be reserved for invalid/expired key. 403 for forbidden/permission mismatch.

maria.g: Will write doc language. Examples would help. Quick snippet proposal:
```http
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <KEY>
X-Org-ID: org-789
X-Project-ID: proj-12  # optional
```
Resolution algorithm we propose: 1) If `X-Org-ID` present, attempt to resolve org; 2) verify key has access to that org — if no access => 403 + `auth_mismatch`; 3) if `X-Org-ID` absent, infer org from key; 4) if neither inferrable => 401 (missing auth).

ryan: What about `X-Project-ID` when present but key is org-scoped? Should project header be validated against org? We should verify that project belongs to resolved org, otherwise 403.

devon: Also call out legacy header `X-Workspace` we've been tolerating. Plan: accept it during deprecation period, but log `legacy_header` tag and emit warning header `X-Deprecation: X-Workspace will be removed` in responses.

aj: For rotation: when rotating keys, there will be a short window where old key and new key both valid. No change to fallback rules. But add a telemetry field `rotation_active=true` for requests that hit the rotation cohort. ops can then track regressions.

infra-bot: Deploy note: canary rollout for the enforcement change will be `eng-platform` -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h. Will emit alert if 5xx or auth-related 4xx spikes > 0.5% of traffic.

maria.g: One more tricky case: proxies that strip `Authorization` and set their own `X-Forwarded-Auth` or pass along `x-original-auth`. We should explicitly ban relying on `X-Forwarded-Auth` for authorization unless it's from a trusted gateway. In private deployments, customers can opt into gateway-trust list. For hosted API default: ignore `X-Forwarded-Auth` unless gateway certificate validated.

aj: Good call. Add this rule: only `Authorization` and `X-Org-ID` and `X-Project-ID` are first-class; everything else is secondary and requires explicit trust config.

sophia: Will the SDKs be updated to stop inferring org from API key when `X-Org-ID` is present? We should push patch to JS/Python SDKs to make behavior explicit and emit a console warning if key-org and header-org mismatch.

maria.g: Yes — PR incoming. I'll include the exact error codes: `401` -> `invalid_key`, `403` -> `auth_mismatch`, `403` -> `project_not_in_org`, `401` -> `missing_auth`. Also responses should include `error_hint` with short text and `error_tags` array for telemetry.

devon: Example responses: 
```json
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "auth_mismatch",
  "error_hint": "X-Org-ID (org-789) not permitted for provided key",
  "error_tags": ["auth_mismatch","org_provided"]
}
```

aj: Minor: ensure we don't leak org existence in the hint for 403s beyond necessary. Keep messages generic in prod while retaining detailed logs internally. Maybe `error_hint` public: "organization mismatch" and internal logs get the full detail.

maria.g: Noted — doc will separate public vs internal error_hint.

ryan: For e2e checks, can we add a small postman collection or curl matrix to the PR? Needed cases: explicit header matching key, header mismatching key, no header+valid key, no header+no key.

maria.g: Yep. I'll add curl examples and a tiny pytest to run against staging. Example curl matrix:
```bash
# header wins, matches key
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY_A" -H "X-Org-ID: org-A" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# header wins, mismatch -> expect 403
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY_A" -H "X-Org-ID: org-B" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# no header, key-scoped org
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY_A" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# no auth -> expect 401
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

infra-bot: Test plan ticket created: INF-4123. Canary schedule added.

aj: OK let's do this: maria, draft doc and PR with tests + SDK note. devon & ryan to review, infra to schedule canary. Sophia to coordinate SDK runtime warnings.

maria.g: Will do. Ping me if you want the deprecation window shorter/longer. Starting with 90 days for `X-Workspace` legacy header deprecation. :thumbsup:

sophia: I'll open SDK PRs after doc lands.

aj: Thanks everyone. Closing thread after PR link posted. :eyes:
